title: Nearest Neighbors
outcome: By the end, I can explain nearest neighbors using a traced example and a stated limitation.
scenario: Let a nearest-neighbour picture show each distance before voting.
given: Training: A length 2 healthy; B length8 spotted; C length11 spotted. Query length5 cm. Distance is absolute difference; ties use alphabetically earlier ID.
All inputs and outcomes in this worked example are invented classroom data; no real model run is claimed.

steps.label: Apply k=1 rule
steps.detail: A and B tie nearest; declared ID tie-break chooses A, predicting healthy.

steps.label: Compare k=3
steps.detail: All three vote: two spotted and one healthy, so k=3 predicts spotted.

explanation: Read the picture in order. All three vote: two spotted and one healthy, so k=3 predicts spotted. The arrows show which recorded input or intermediate result each decision uses. Explain the deciding step aloud before checking the changed case; pointing to the final answer alone does not show how it follows.

counterfactual.change: Move the query to length7 cm.
counterfactual.prediction: k=1 predicts spotted from B, distance1; k=3 remains spotted.
counterfactual.reason: Distances become 5, 1, 4 cm, so the nearest tie disappears.

student_task: Why is the k=1 outcome at length5 not uniquely determined without a tie rule? Point to the relevant step in the picture, then write the changed result and the rule or evidence that supports it.
teacher_answer: A healthy and B spotted are equally near. The declared alphabetical rule resolves the otherwise ambiguous one-neighbour selection. Changed-case check: k=1 predicts spotted from B, distance1; k=3 remains spotted. Distances become 5, 1, 4 cm, so the nearest tie disappears.
project_evidence: For your Responsible Plant Classifier, save the input, procedure, observed result and limitation of this check. Label this worked example as practice; use a different, previously unreviewed case when checking independent understanding.
limits: Length alone is a toy feature, not a disease diagnosis. Distance choices and feature scaling can change neighbours.
review_note: Reviewed Nearest Neighbors against the assigned lesson pack and its reserved independent case. Added a different explicit worked scenario, an auditable trace and a changed-input check; preserved the original curriculum and assessment boundary.

mini_visual.title: One-dimensional neighbours shown along length axis
mini_visual.metric: Absolute length difference; ties use alphabetically earlier ID
